gaps.sentence: Could you ___ me a favour and close the window?
gaps.explanation: do somebody a favour is the fixed collocation; 'make a favour' is a common error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ a loud argument in the garden last night.
gaps.explanation: have an argument (with somebody) is the fixed collocation for quarrelling.

gaps.sentence: The critics ___ praise on the young violinist.
gaps.explanation: 'Heap praise on' = give a great deal of praise.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.
